request.spec:
RUN should cover more ground. RUN now runs from zero up to and including one hundred and
ninety-nine, and PEAK only starts at two hundred. EBB is unchanged.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
RUN should cover more ground. RUN now runs from zero up to and including one hundred and
ninety-nine, and PEAK only starts at two hundred. EBB is unchanged.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
RUN now covers torque from 0 up to and including 199, and PEAK starts at 200. EBB is still everything below zero. `bin/e2e` passes.

- **Server:** the phase is worked out only in `Person.getPhase()` (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/people/Person.java:454`), so the fix was changing the RUN cutoff there from `<= 99` to `<= 199`. I updated the comment above it to match.
- **Front end:** it just displays the phase it gets from the server, so only the comment in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts:13` needed updating.
- **Stored data:** nothing changed. Phase is calculated when it's read, not saved, so the seed and read-back endpoints didn't need any changes.
